emails.subject: fifty days
emails.text:
Fifty days.

That's what stands between today and November 3rd.

Fifty days to knock every door in San Francisco.

Fifty days to make sure working families, immigrants, and renters have someone in Congress who's actually fought for them.

Fifty days to finish what we started.

I've spent two decades doing this work as a public servant — not with press conferences, but with budgets that kept clinics open and protected the people this city depends on. I've also stood up to the billionaires and big corporations to deliver for working people. I'm ready to take this fight to Washington.

Fifty days is enough time to win this race — if we use every single one of them. It's enough time for a volunteer to have the conversation that changes a voter's mind. It's enough time for your contribution today to fund one more canvass shift, one more mail piece, one more chance to reach someone who hasn't made up their mind yet.

I don't take a single day of this for granted. Will you chip in $3 to help me make the most of the fifty we have left?

Donate >>

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: The author of Medicare for All picked a side
emails.text:
Big news, barallies: Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal just endorsed Connie for Congress.

Gazetteer San Francisco: Pramila Jayapal endorses Connie Chan
"Connie Chan is the kind of progressive fighter we need in Congress: she stands with working families, takes on corporate power, and knows that health care is a right, not a privilege," Jayapal said

Jayapal wrote Medicare for All. She knows better than almost anyone in Washington what it takes to actually deliver universal health care, and she says Connie is who she needs standing with her in Congress.

As a reminder, Connie has pledged to co-sponsor the Medicare for All Act on day one. No copays, no deductibles, no more private insurers deciding whether your care gets approved. And as Budget Chair, she secured $400 million to shield San Francisco's public hospital and clinics from Trump's cuts.

Our opponent Scott Wiener, on the other hand, has a different approach to health care – one that didn't sit well with the people who deliver it. The California Nurses Association warned his health care bill would mean more bureaucratic delay, not less. They called it a "complete betrayal."

Nurses know how much our families deserve universal health care – that's why they joined Congresswoman Jayapal in endorsing Connie.

Endorsements like this don't happen by accident. They happen because people like you have spent months building a campaign serious enough to earn them. Will you chip in $3 to help send a real Medicare for All champion to Congress?

Donate >>

- Team Connie

emails.subject: An AI safety researcher just quit. Here's his warning:
emails.text:
barallies,

This week, a researcher who helped build frontier AI systems at companies like Anthropic and OpenAI quit – and posted publicly about why. He's warning that this technology could be dangerous for humankind.

A safety lead at Anthropic didn't dispute him. He said there's a real chance – more than 1 in 10 – AI "could kill all humans" within the next decade.

This isn't a warning from critics on the outside. It's coming from the people building it.

This is a big reason why I just signed the AI PACT: a public commitment to stand up to an industry that thinks it should get to write its own rules. No industry this powerful should get to police itself. Not on safety. Not on jobs. Not on how it treats the people whose voices it can now fabricate with a few keystrokes.

I've seen firsthand how this industry acts when no one's watching. Just a few weeks ago, Scott Wiener's campaign used AI to impersonate me – and only backed down after public pressure from Nancy Pelosi and other leaders. Wiener's chatbot was powered by the same AI company that has spent $500,000 to support his campaign.

Scott Wiener took the industry's money and used AI against me. I chose to hold that same industry accountable instead. Will you chip in $3 so we can outwork the special interest money backing my opponent?

Donate >>

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: barallies, this is who's funding the attacks on Connie
emails.text:
barallies, here's what's happening:

A new mailer attacking Connie is hitting mailboxes across San Francisco – paid for by Abundant Future, the Super PAC that took $500,000 from Anthropic.

This isn't the first swing they've taken either: Abundant Future has already spent more than $500,000 in this general election alone.

Then there's GrowUSA, pledging another $400,000. It's a GrowSF offshoot, backed by the same crypto and Big Tech money that's tried to control San Francisco politics for years. Add it up, and millions of dollars from billionaires and corporate money are lining up to try to buy this seat for Scott Wiener before November.

Every dollar they spend attacking Connie is proof her message is landing. Will you chip in $3 to help us answer back before this mailer reaches every voter in the district?

Donate $3

While Wiener's side counts dollars, our coalition keeps growing.

Every week, more volunteers pick up a clipboard, more first-time donors chip in $5 or $10, and more San Franciscans decide CA-11 isn't for sale. That's not something you can just write a check for and buy.

Will you chip in $3 today to help close the gap Wiener's tech billionaires and AI brokers are counting on? Every contribution is proof their money can't buy what we've built here.

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: "Yes We Chan" hats now available!
emails.text:
barallies,

From tees and beanies to tote bags and our highly requested "Yes We Chan" hats — we've got everything you need to rep this campaign wherever you go.

Connie Chan HQ

emails.subject: Labor Day message from Connie's campaign manager
emails.sender: Rudy Gonzalez, via Connie Chan for Congress
emails.text:
barallies,

This is Rudy Gonzalez. I've spent my career in the labor movement — first as a Teamster at 18, then leading the San Francisco Labor Council, and now as secretary-treasurer of the SF Building & Construction Trades Council.

I didn't expect to take a leave of absence from my work at the Building Trades to run a congressional campaign. But when Connie asked, I didn't hesitate.

I want to tell you why.

I've watched Connie show up for working people in this city for years. Not just at endorsement time — at the picket line. At the budget table, fighting to protect union jobs when City Hall wanted to cut them. In the halls of power, standing up for the nurses, teachers, firefighters, hotel workers, and building trades members who actually make San Francisco run.

She's been there, again and again, when it counted.

This Labor Day, I want to say something that gets lost in the noise of a big congressional race: the most powerful thing we have isn't a TV ad or a super PAC. It's people. Organized people, showing up together, having real conversations with their neighbors. That's how labor wins. And that's how this campaign is going to win. Scott Wiener has the billionaires. He has the crypto donors and the corporate PACs. We have something better — a movement of working people who believe San Francisco shouldn't be for sale.

But movements need people to show up. This Labor Day weekend, I'm asking you to join us — knock a door, make some calls, show a neighbor why this race matters. If you can't make it out, a contribution to keep our organizers on the ground can go just as far.

This is how we win. Not by outspending them — by outworking them.

In solidarity,

Rudy Gonzalez
Campaign Manager

Donate | Volunteer

emails.subject: One month until ballots drop
emails.text:

In one month, ballots will start arriving in mailboxes. We need your help this month making sure everyone is registered to vote, has a plan to vote, and is voting for Connie Chan.

[Photo: Connie and a supporter voting in June. Make sure you have a plan to vote for this November's election!]

Our campaign isn't powered by billionaires or corporate donors. It's powered by working people like you, and we know that together our people-powered campaign can and will overcome the corporate cash being poured into this race. Can you join us for a volunteer shift to get the word out about Connie's agenda and goals?

[Photo: Connie and a supporter at the Noe Valley Night Market. Can you join us for a volunteer shift this week to help spread the word about Connie?]

Saturday we will be knocking doors at McCoppin Square Park. RSVP here

Sunday we will be canvassing in the Mission. Meet at our campaign headquarters at 3043 24th Street. RSVP here to join.

emails.subject: Checking in one more time, barallies
emails.text:
I'm glad I caught you, barallies.

I'm writing one last time today because our August fundraising deadline hits at midnight, and we're still short of the goal we set for this month.

I won't pretend that doesn't matter. Every dollar we raise goes straight toward keeping our volunteers knocking doors and having real conversations with voters across San Francisco – the kind of work that will actually decide this race.

If you've been meaning to give this month and haven't yet, this is your last chance to do so before August ends. Can you chip in $3 before the clock runs out tonight?

Thank you,

Connie

emails.subject: Still just $1
emails.text:
$1.

That's what we're asking you to chip in to Connie's campaign today.

Donate $1

Defeating Scott Wiener was never going to be about matching his money. It's about out-organizing him – door-by-door, conversation-by-conversation, across every neighborhood in San Francisco.

That kind of organizing isn't free. Every $1 adds up to real things:

$1 helps keep our volunteers knocking doors across the Sunset, the Mission, Bayview and every corner of this district.

$1 helps us reach voters by text and phone who we'd never find otherwise – and in multiple languages.

$1 proves, one more time, that this campaign is powered by people – not billionaire Super PAC checks.

Scott Wiener has Big Tech, crypto donors, and corporate PACs supporting him. What we have is people like you, showing up again and again, in amounts as small as $1.

With our end-of-month deadline closing in tomorrow, can you chip in $1 to help us keep showing up all the way to November?

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: My opponent’s “MAGA fan club”
emails.text:
barallies,

Scott Wiener likes to brag about his "MAGA fan club" of right-wing critics.

But let's talk about his actual fan club.

There are two super PACs spending big right now to put him in Congress. One is funded by Big Tech and crypto special interests. Another – GrowUSA – is bankrolled by a network of billionaire corporate donors.

When you look at who's behind this network, some of the same executives writing big checks to boost Scott have written big checks to boost Donald Trump.

That's Scott's real MAGA fan club.

While billionaire donors spend whatever it takes to buy this seat, we're building a movement powered by nurses, teachers, firefighters, union members, tenants, and working families who actually make San Francisco run.

My opponent can have the Trump donors and billionaires.

I'll take the people.

Our end-of-month deadline hits in two days and we still need some help hitting our goal. Will you chip in $3 to prove that people-power beats big money?

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: Here's the latest in the race for CA-11.
emails.text:
barallies,

In a moment, we're going to ask you to make a grassroots donation of $3 to our campaign. But before we do, here's what you need to know right now:

The latest poll has us within striking distance. It's 45-40 in Scott Wiener's favor, but we've seen an upward swing of 10-points since the primary. Connie has the momentum.

A new super PAC funded by billionaire tech executives and Trump donors announced $400,000 in new ads to boost Wiener's campaign. That should tell you everything you need to know about the interests propping him up.

We set a goal of raising $25,000 in online donations before the end of this week to keep pace. As it stands, we're coming up a bit short.

If you've been watching this race and waiting for when your dollars would make a huge impact — this is it. Please chip in $3 today to help us close the gap on our goal.

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: I'm not who they expected
emails.text:
barallies,

We're just days away from our end-of-month deadline, and we need your support. You can chip in $3 before it hits, and let me explain.

People have asked me this: Can you really handle Congress?

I'm an immigrant. I speak with an accent. I'm a working mom.

And for a long time, that was enough for some people to question whether I belonged in rooms where decisions were made. Now as we face the halls of Congress it continues to be a question. But when they see a white man in a suit, there's no question.

But for women, and women of color? The standard is different.

We have to prove ourselves over and over again.
We have to be better than great.
We have to be perfect.

That standard is almost impossible. So I'm flipping this question on its head: Can Congress handle me?

I'm not going to Washington to fit in. I'm going to fight for working families, I'm going to stand up to big money, and I'm going to bring the voices of San Francisco to the forefront – whether the status quo is ready for it or not.

So right now, we need your help to prove that this campaign can go toe-to-toe against these standards AND WIN. If you're with me, if you chip in $3 before our end-of-month deadline, your contribution will help send a message that we aren't backing down.

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: Scott Wiener hurls attacks at Speaker Pelosi and Ro Khanna.
emails.text:
Scott Wiener seems to have forgotten he's running against Connie. He's now going after all the people who stand with her.

Politico reported this morning that his flailing campaign has been attacking both Nancy Pelosi and Ro Khanna – two respected leaders in our party – ever since Ro stood alongside Connie at a union hall here in San Francisco.

This isn't new for Scott. As Rep. Khanna put it, Wiener has been "echoing false right-wing attacks on Speaker Pelosi for over a year."

He'll do or say anything to win. And it's starting to show.

Meanwhile, Connie is doing what she's always done: knocking doors, building a coalition of labor, educators, and working families, and staying focused on the fight that actually matters.

Lashing out isn't a winning – or a governing – strategy. This is what desperation looks like.

With our end-of-month deadline hitting August 31st, every dollar is a vote for the kind of politics Connie represents. Will you chip in $3 before midnight on the 31st to help fuel this movement all the way to November?

Thank you,

Team Connie

emails.subject: The only model of politics I trust
emails.text:
Six days left in August, barallies.

Every month, my fundraising team sets a goal -- it's what tells us whether we can keep paying the people knocking doors across this district, keep the phones running, and keep our campaign visible in every neighborhood. That number is the difference between a field program that runs strong into November and one that has to pull back.

For this month, we're not quite to our goal yet.

I grew up in a family that had no political power and no connections. Nobody handed us anything. What we had was each other -- and the people who showed up when it counted. That's the only model of politics I trust, and the only way I know how to run a campaign.

This final week isn't about panic. It's about continuing what we said we'd do. A campaign like this doesn't run on a handful of big checks -- it runs on hundreds of people deciding, month after month, that this is worth a few dollars. That's what gets us to the number we need by the 31st.

Can you help us get there? $3 or whatever you're able to give is exactly what we need to get across the finish line.

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: Town Hall Recap
emails.text:
Dear barallies,

Last week, we held a town hall with Congressman Ro Khanna and the California Working Families Party to discuss some of the most important issues for voters.

How do we fight back against Trump? How do we prevent families from being priced out of the Bay Area? How do we fund priorities nationwide like Medicare for All, universal childcare, and Free City College?

The answer is pretty simple: We put working families before corporations. We make sure billionaires pay their fair share. We stop spending $1.5 trillion on war, and invest that money back into our communities.

I am grateful that Congressman Ro Khanna and California Working Families Party Director Jorge Contreras joined us at our town hall to talk with voters on how to stand up for working Californians in Washington D.C.

Our worker-centric policies are why corporate interests are spending big to prevent us from winning this seat. But I know we've got the people-power to beat them.

Can you join us for a volunteer shift this week to help spread the word about Connie?

Join us for a volunteer shift this week!

Saturday, August 29th we will be canvassing in Glen Park at 10am. We will meet at the entrance of Glen Canyon Park on Chenery & Elk Streets. RSVP here.

Sunday we will be canvassing in the Mission. Meet at our campaign headquarters at 3043 24th Street. RSVP here to join.

Every Tuesday and Thursday join us as we phonebank voters from our Campaign HQ.

Interested in visibility? Swing by the office (3043 24th St, San Francisco, CA 94110) anytime between 10am-6pm on weekdays and we'll get you set up to do visibility at a farmers market, or put up signs in your local neighborhood corridor.

Thanks for all your support.

In solidarity,
Team Connie

emails.subject: I want to show you something in his own campaign's filings:
emails.text:
barallies, this is a long, but important email about the troubling stories emerging about my opponent's campaign finances. I hope you'll take a moment to read this whole message, then chip in $3 to help us keep running our campaign the right way.

For decades, strict firewall rules kept congressional campaigns from coordinating directly with super PACs. That wall existed for a reason: super PACs can raise unlimited corporate cash, and keeping them separate was the last line of defense against billionaires and special interests outright bankrolling a candidate's campaign.

In 2024, the FEC created a loophole. And Scott Wiener's campaign didn't just take full advantage — they went even further.

FEC filings show the super PAC behind Scott has been paying the same staffers to work in the same office at the same time under the same leadership as Wiener's congressional campaign.

I'll let you decide what it says about a candidate when the very first thing he does with a weaker rule is test its limits.

This is the difference between us. I don't take corporate PAC money. I never have. Every dollar in this campaign is one I can look you in the eye about — raised from people who believe in our mission, not special interests who expect something in return.

Money can buy ads. It can buy staff time twice over if you're clever about which entity cuts the check. What it can't buy is the trust we've built door-to-door, house by house, across this district.

Will you chip in $3 to help us keep building this campaign the honest way?

In solidarity,

Connie

emails.subject: before you scroll past this
emails.text:
We wanted to make sure you saw Connie's note, barallies.

She's spent two decades fighting for working families in San Francisco. Her opponent, Scott Wiener, took Big Tech money and let an AI chatbot mock her accent, her background, even her citizenship – then plastered it on billboards across the city.

When Nancy Pelosi and leaders across the state called him out, Scott attacked them. Then he shrugged the whole thing off as a "political experiment" that just "missed the mark."

That's not an apology. That's not leadership.

This race is neck and neck and will come down to grassroots support from folks like you in 94114. Will you chip in $3 right now?

Donate $3

Thank you,

Team Connie

---------- Forwarded message ----------

barallies,

I want to tell you something Scott Wiener's AI chatbot said about me.

It mocked my accent as "so thick I can barely understand myself." It made jokes about my birth certificate being "tied up in committee." It claimed my citizenship status is "classified." And it was plastered on billboards across San Francisco.

I came to this city as a first-generation American immigrant from Hong Kong. I built my life here. I raised my family here. And I have spent two decades fighting for the working families of San Francisco.

That is what drives me and who I fight for every day. That is who Scott Wiener chose to mock.

Under pressure from Nancy Pelosi and leaders across our city and state, he eventually took it down. But he never took real responsibility – he first doubled down by blaming our campaign and said the political experiment just "missed the mark."

I'll let you decide what that says about his character and judgement.

Recent polling has this race neck and neck, and we have a clear path to victory in November. Scott Wiener has the AI industry's money behind him. We have you – will you chip in $3 right now to power our campaign for Congress?

In solidarity,

Connie
(The real me)

emails.subject: Another super PAC is jumping in for Scott Wiener.
emails.text:
barallies,

The corporate cavalry just arrived for Scott Wiener.

A brand-new super PAC called GrowUSA launched with one purpose: a billionaire bailout for Scott's campaign. They're starting with $400,000 — and they've made clear they'll spend significantly more before November.

This is what it looks like when Big Tech and corporate money decide they want to buy an election because their candidate is in trouble. GrowUSA is an offshoot of GrowSF, the same crypto, tech, and venture capital backed outfit that has tried to sway San Francisco politics for years.

We can't match a super PAC dollar for dollar. But we've never had to — because we've built this campaign door by door, neighborhood by neighborhood, in every language spoken in this city. That's what they can't buy.

$400,000 is just the opening bid, and every day we don't respond is another day that money hits airwaves and mailboxes unchallenged. Will you chip in $3 right now to make sure their money doesn't drown out our movement?

In solidarity,

Team Connie

emails.subject: The stakes just changed.
emails.sender: Adam Schiff, via Connie Chan for Congress
emails.text:
barallies,

Donald Trump fired every remaining commissioner of the federal agency that helps states run secure elections.

By email. Effective immediately. Just months before the midterms.

Days earlier, his Justice Department announced it was deploying election monitors to battleground states and Democratic strongholds — and threatened election officials in all 50 states with criminal prosecution.

Fired the referees. Sent in his own watchers. Threatened the people who count the votes.

I spent years as a federal prosecutor. I know a pattern of intent when I see one. This isn't election security — it's an attempt to seize control of our elections before a single ballot is cast.

There is one check on his abuse of power that Trump cannot fire and cannot intimidate: a Democratic Congress.

That's why we're scaling up our operations right now — expanding the infrastructure it will take to hold him accountable and retake the Congress.

barallies, will you split a contribution between Connie Chan and me to help us defend our elections and win back Congress?

Trump is betting that Americans won't notice. That we won't fight back.

He's wrong on both counts. I've stood up to him before — through impeachment, through censure, through my service on the January 6th Committee, through every smear he's thrown at me — and I'm not about to stop now.

Thank you for your support.

— Adam
